extra.message: Webhook shared secret stored in cleartext

metadata.proof: The Webhook model stores the shared secret used to sign webhook payloads as a plaintext VARCHAR column in the database. Unlike ApiKey keys which are SHA-256 hashed (see create_api_key in integrations.py), the webhook secret has no hashing or encryption. A database compromise exposes all webhook secrets, allowing attackers to forge signed webhook payloads that downstream systems would accept as legitimate.

extra.message: Webhook secret returned in API responses

metadata.proof: WebhookBase defines the 'secret' field, and WebhookOut inherits it. The GET /api/integrations/webhooks endpoint returns list[WebhookOut], and POST /api/integrations/webhooks returns WebhookOut as well. This means the raw webhook shared secret is transmitted over the API to any PROPERTY_ADMIN user, increasing the exposure surface beyond the database alone.

extra.message: DocumentOut exposes internal filesystem path

metadata.proof: DocumentOut includes the server-internal file_path field, which is returned to clients by GET /api/documents/{id} and GET /api/documents. This leaks the upload directory structure (e.g., /var/data/uploads/documents/...), aiding further path-traversal or direct-file-access attacks.

extra.message: CSV formula injection in payments export

metadata.citation: writer.writerow([p.id, p.tenant_id, p.lease_id, p.amount, p.due_date, p.paid_date, p.status.value, p.payment_method])
metadata.proof: The payment_method free-text field (max_length=50, set via PaymentRecordCreate/PaymentRecordUpdate) is written directly into the CSV without any sanitization. A PROPERTY_ADMIN or PROPERTY_MANAGER who sets payment_method to a value starting with '=', '+', '-', or '@' will cause formula execution when the exported CSV is opened in Excel or LibreOffice.

extra.message: CSV formula injection in rent roll export

metadata.proof: The rent roll export includes tenant full_name (from lease.tenant.user.full_name) and property/building/unit names written directly into CSV via csv.DictWriter.writerows. The tenant full_name is user-controlled input (set during registration/update, max_length=255, no sanitization). A tenant who sets their name to a formula injection payload (e.g., '=CMD|...') will cause formula execution when the CSV is opened.

extra.message: CSV formula injection in inspections export

metadata.proof: The inspections export includes inspector full_name (from i.inspector.full_name) and property/unit names written directly into CSV without sanitization. The inspector full_name is user-controlled. A formula injection payload in this field executes when the CSV is opened in a spreadsheet application.

extra.message: Broken tenant ownership check compares User.id to Tenant.id

metadata.proof: SOURCE: current_user.id comes from the JWT token and is the users.id primary key. SINK: can_view_maintenance_ticket compares it to MaintenanceTicket.tenant_id, which is a ForeignKey to tenants.id — a completely different table with an independent auto-increment sequence. A tenant whose User.id coincidentally matches another tenant's Tenant.id can view that other tenant's tickets. This affects GET/PATCH /api/maintenance/{id}, POST /api/maintenance/{id}/comments, GET /api/maintenance/{id}/comments, POST /api/maintenance/{id}/photos, GET /api/maintenance/{id}/photos, and GET /api/integrations/status/tickets/{id}.

extra.message: Cross-tenant document access via unconditional True for PropertyManager on un-scoped documents

metadata.proof: SOURCE: user-supplied document id in GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/documents/{id} and GET /api/documents/{id}/download. SINK: can_view_document returns True unconditionally for any PropertyManager when doc.unit_id is None (line 97). The list endpoint (documents.py:33-34) also includes Document.unit_id == None unconditionally for managers. A manager of Property A can read, modify, or list global documents (no unit_id) belonging to Property B with no property-level scoping.

extra.message: PropertyManager user listing exposes all maintenance workers system-wide

metadata.proof: SOURCE: current_user.role == PROPERTY_MANAGER triggers manager branch in list_users. SINK: the filter adds all MAINTENANCE_WORKER users with no property-scope check (line 45). A manager of Property A can enumerate every maintenance worker in the system, including those assigned to Property B.

extra.message: Login response distinguishes disabled accounts from invalid credentials

metadata.proof: SOURCE: user-supplied email and password in POST /api/auth/login. SINK: a valid email with correct password for a disabled account returns HTTP 403 'Account is disabled' (line 37), while a non-existent email or wrong password returns HTTP 401 'Invalid email or password' (line 34). An attacker can enumerate valid registered emails and identify which accounts are disabled.

extra.message: Password reset confirmation does not revoke existing JWT sessions

metadata.proof: SOURCE: POST /api/auth/password-reset-confirm with user-supplied token and new_password. SINK: the password hash is updated (line 82) but no existing access tokens or cookie sessions are invalidated. JWT tokens issued before the password change remain valid until expiry (8 hours per config.py), because get_current_user only decodes the token and loads the user — it never checks a token version or password hash. An attacker holding a pre-reset token can continue accessing the API.

extra.message: Unbounded file read in unit CSV import causes memory exhaustion

metadata.proof: SOURCE: user-supplied UploadFile to POST /api/imports/units. SINK: file.file.read() loads the entire upload into a single string with no size validation against settings.max_upload_size (10MB). A multi-gigabyte CSV can exhaust server memory.

extra.message: File uploads do not enforce maximum size limit, enabling disk exhaustion

metadata.proof: SOURCE: UploadFile passed to save_upload_file from POST /api/documents, /api/maintenance/{id}/photos, and /api/inspections/{id}/photos. SINK: settings.max_upload_size is defined as 10MB but never enforced (line 22); the upload is streamed to disk with no size cap, allowing disk exhaustion DoS.

extra.message: Integration ticket status endpoint uses broken tenant ownership check

metadata.proof: SOURCE: ticket_id path parameter in GET /api/integrations/status/tickets/{ticket_id}. SINK: can_view_maintenance_ticket compares MaintenanceTicket.tenant_id (ForeignKey to tenants.id) directly against user.id (users.id) — two entirely different ID spaces (line 116 and permissions.py:74-75). Tenants can never view their own tickets (tenant_id != user.id), but may access other tenants' tickets when ID values coincidentally match.
